events.name: Greenville County Republican Party Quarterly Meeting
events.event: The county party's regular quarterly meeting, with local, state and federal candidates appearing.
events.location: Greenville Tech Campus, Multipurpose Room in the Prisma Health Center building, Greenville
events.notes: Doors open at 5:30 pm and the meeting starts at 6:30 pm, running to 8:30 pm. This is a partisan organisation's own meeting. Check the party's notice before setting out.

events.name: SC Governor Debate
events.event: Alan Wilson (R) and Jermaine Johnson (D) meet in the televised debate for the governor of South Carolina.
events.notes: Runs 7:00 pm to 8:00 pm and is streamed live by WIS. Whether the studio admits an audience has not been published, so treat that as unknown rather than settled either way.

events.name: SC-04 Congressional Debate
events.event: William Timmons (R), the incumbent, and Courtney McClain (D) meet in the televised debate for South Carolina's 4th Congressional District.
events.notes: Runs 7:00 pm to 8:00 pm and is broadcast by FOX Carolina. SC-04 covers the Greenville area, so this is the Upstate's own congressional race.

events.name: SCETV U.S. Senate Debate
events.event: Dr. Annie Andrews (D), Sen. Darline Graham (R) and Dr. Kasie Whitener (L) meet in the televised debate for the United States Senate seat, streamed from Columbia by SCETV.
events.notes: SCETV published the 7:00 pm start on 25 September. It is broadcast and streamed live across SCETV's television and radio networks. Three candidates are confirmed participants, not two.

events.name: Early Voting (in person)
events.event: In-person early voting runs for two weeks at early voting centers across South Carolina. Polls are open 8:30 am to 6:00 pm, and closed on Sunday 25 October.
events.location: Early voting centers in your county, statewide
events.notes: You may use any early voting center in your county, not only the one nearest your home. Check scvotes.gov, or your county's election office, before travelling.

events.name: General Election
events.event: South Carolina votes for a United States senator, the governor, all seven House of Representatives seats, the state House of Representatives and county offices. Upstate voters also decide SC-04 between William Timmons and Courtney McClain, and SC-03, where Sheri Biggs is the candidate.
events.notes: Polls are open 7:00 am until 7:00 pm. Confirm your polling place with your county election office before you go. If you are in line when the polls close, you are entitled to vote.

events.name: City of Greenwood General Election
events.event: Greenwood holds its own general election on the same day as the state and federal vote, for city offices and any municipal contests on the ballot.
events.notes: Held on the same day as the state and federal election. Greenwood is the county seat of Greenwood County. Confirm your polling place with Greenwood County.

events.name: Greenville County Election Certification
events.event: The Greenville County Voter Registration and Election Board meets to certify the results of the 3 November general election.
events.location: 225 S. Pleasantburg Drive, Suite B-10, Greenville
events.notes: 11:00 am, taken from the board's own published 2026 meeting schedule, which lists this as the meeting that certifies the general election. Agendas and times are published in advance and can change, so check the board's notice before travelling.

events.name: Greenville County Council Meeting
events.event: A regular public meeting of Greenville County Council in Council Chambers. Committee meetings are generally held in the Committee Room at County Square.
events.location: Council Chambers, 301 University Ridge (County Square), Greenville
events.notes: 6:00 pm, from the county's own projected 2026 meeting schedule. That schedule states all dates are tentative and subject to cancellation, so confirm against the county's agenda listing before setting out.

events.name: Vardry McBee's Children and Grandchildren
events.event: A Greenville County Historical Society lecture by Dr. Robert Benedict on the children and grandchildren of Vardry McBee.
events.location: Downtown Presbyterian Church, 435 W Washington Street, Greenville
events.notes: Runs 6:30 pm to 8:00 pm on a Wednesday evening. Free to Historical Society members; tickets for non-members are 15 dollars.

events.name: SC State Election Commission Meeting
events.event: A regular meeting of the State Election Commission, the body that oversees election administration across South Carolina, at its Columbia office.
events.notes: 10:00 am, the Commission's standard start time unless a notice says otherwise. Its published notices state that meetings are subject to change up to 24 hours beforehand, so confirm before travelling to Columbia.

events.name: The People Who Lived Here 10,000 Years Ago
events.event: A Greenville County Historical Society lecture by James T. Hammond on the people who lived in this part of the Upstate ten thousand years ago.
events.location: Downtown Presbyterian Church, 435 W Washington Street, Greenville
events.notes: Runs 6:30 pm to 8:00 pm on a Wednesday evening. Free to Historical Society members; tickets for non-members are 15 dollars.

events.name: Greenville County Schools Board Meeting
events.event: The Board of Trustees of Greenville County Schools meets in regular session to set district policy and conduct public business.
events.location: Central Office, 301 E. Camperdown Way, Greenville
events.notes: 6:00 pm. The district's board portal lists an executive session earlier the same evening, which is not open to the public; the regular meeting is. Agendas are published on the portal before each meeting. This falls on the same evening as a County Council meeting, which is a different body at a different address.

events.name: Greenville County Schools Board Meeting
events.event: The Board of Trustees of Greenville County Schools meets in regular session to set district policy and conduct public business.
events.location: Central Office, 301 E. Camperdown Way, Greenville
events.notes: 6:00 pm. A Committee of the Whole meeting and an executive session are listed earlier the same day on the district's portal; the regular meeting is the public one. This is an earlier date in the month than the board's usual pattern, so take the published date rather than the habit.

events.name: Greenville County Schools Board Meeting
events.event: The Board of Trustees of Greenville County Schools meets in regular session to set district policy and conduct public business.
events.location: Central Office, 301 E. Camperdown Way, Greenville
events.notes: 6:00 pm. An executive session is listed earlier the same evening on the district's portal, which is not open to the public; the regular meeting is. Agendas are published before each meeting.

pageNote.heading: After the election: certification, and what is not on the ballot
paragraphs: Results from the 3 November general election are certified in stages rather than declared final on the night. County boards act first: Greenville County's Voter Registration and Election Board certifies its count on 6 November, and the State Board of Canvassers later certifies the statewide result.

No further election follows in the Upstate. The State Election Commission's master calendar for 2026 lists no election anywhere in the state between 3 November and 1 December, when the Town of Paxville in Clarendon County holds its municipal general election. There is no November runoff.

Public business continues through the winter. Greenville County Council's published schedule lists regular meetings on 17 November and 1 December at 6:00 pm in Council Chambers. The county school board meets at 6:00 pm on 17 November, 8 December and 26 January at the district's Central Office, and the Historical Society's lecture series runs monthly through to May.
